title: oneb digest output
description: Machine-readable contract for the JSON files render writes. A file is either a DailyDigest (<cbsa>.<yyyy-mm-dd>.json) or a WeeklyDigest (<cbsa>.weekly.json). This schema is the exchange artifact for the UI layer; the authoritative enforcement lives in render/src/oneb_render/contract.py (validate_day / validate_week) and the prose contract in openspec/specs/digest-output-contract/. Objects are intentionally open (additive fields are safe to ignore). Render applies NO per-appeal display count: are_you_ok, conversation_starters and you_should_know are complete ordered candidate sets in both the daily and the weekly file, so the consuming UI owns how many of each a reader sees and must bound them itself.

IsoOffsetDateTime.description: ISO 8601 timestamp carrying a numeric UTC offset (e.g. -05:00). A 'Z'/UTC designator is NOT allowed: the UI reads the wall-clock time straight off the string, so a Z value would render the wrong local hour.

Image.description: Lead image, or null when the item has none.

Article.description: A story card. Emitted in are_you_ok, conversation_starters, you_should_know (and their weekly counterparts).

summary.description: One-line editorial blurb (may be empty). In a weekly item that threads several articles this is the multi-day arc summary.

uid.description: Stable, opaque per-item feedback identity, minted at fetch. Present on every Article: fetch refuses to emit an item without one.

logo.description: Optional outlet logo URL, joined from the outlet registry by source. Absent when the outlet has no known logo.

description.description: Optional plain-text snippet (<=280 chars, no HTML/markup). Absent when the item has no blurb.

thread.description: Weekly only: the contributing daily Articles behind a clustered multi-day item.

WeatherAlert.description: One active, allow-listed NWS alert. The array is ordered most-severe first; render every entry unconditionally (significance filtering is upstream). A multi-day alert appears on every UTC day of its active window.

event.description: Canonical NWS event name, e.g. 'Heat Advisory', rendered verbatim.

area.description: Collapsed metro county label: a county name; 'A & B'; 'A, B +N more'; or 'metro-wide'. May be empty.

severity.description: NWS CAP severity; drives the most-severe-first ordering.

summary.description: Reworded reader-facing summary (may be empty). Redundant with event/area/ends; safe to ignore.

ends.description: When the alert expires, or null if open-ended.

SportsEntry.description: One team's lines for the day (or, in a weekly digest, for the window). The section carries every kept sports item, not only game results, so an entry may cover a trade, an injury or an off-field story alongside scorelines.

scores.description: The team's lines, one per item, in encounter order. Despite the field name these are not necessarily scorelines: a line may read 'signs goalie to extension'. Sports carries no rank, so the order is not an editorial ranking.

are_you_ok.description: Every human 'are you ok' story for the day, in rank order, with no upper bound — the UI applies the display count. Never displaced by weather alerts.

sports.description: The day's kept sports items grouped by team.

WeeklyDigest.description: The trailing-7-day highlight reel (<cbsa>.weekly.json). No weather_alert section.

range.description: Inclusive UTC day window; start <= end.

are_you_ok.description: Bounded upstream by prioritize's weekly selection (6 today) and not re-sliced by render, so the bound may move without a schema change. The UI applies the display count.

conversation_starters.description: Bounded upstream by prioritize's weekly selection (15 today) and not re-sliced by render, so the bound may move without a schema change. The UI applies the display count.

you_should_know.description: Bounded upstream by prioritize's weekly selection (15 today) and not re-sliced by render, so the bound may move without a schema change. The UI applies the display count.

sports.description: Every team's kept sports items across the window, grouped by team.
